items.title: Trust by Context, Not by Design? A Quantitative Study of Data Donation Willingness for Open-Source Civic AI in Switzerland
items.desc: A study of Swiss residents examines the conditions of transparency and user control under which people are willing to donate data to open-source 'civic AI' systems that support democratic participation, weighing the value of improving AI models against residents' expectations of privacy and consent. [arXiv econ.EM, posted 2026-07-23]

sections.name: 📦 Operations & Supply Chain (INFORMS: Management Science, M&SOM, Operations Research)

items.title: Silicon Valley Splits Over Closing the Borders to Chinese A.I.
items.desc: A fight has erupted between Anthropic and OpenAI, which want tighter restrictions on Chinese open-source AI models on safety and IP-theft grounds, and much of the rest of the industry (Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, Google), which signed a letter defending open source; the Trump administration is weighing targeted national-security curbs rather than a blanket ban as Chinese labs like Z.ai and Moonshot catch up. [NYT, 2026-07-25]

items.title: Blockbuster I.P.O.s Are Creating New Millionaires. Philanthropies Want a Cut.
items.desc: As Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX head toward some of the largest IPOs ever, nonprofits and wealth advisers are bracing for a philanthropic windfall estimated between $37 billion and $100 billion a year, driven partly by capital-gains tax incentives and founders' effective-altruism pledges. [NYT DealBook, 2026-07-25]

items.title: We Interviewed A.I. Agents. They Nailed Your Co-Workers' Worst Habits.
items.desc: An executive coach argues that friction in workplace AI adoption stems less from the agents than from poor human management habits, such as vague requests, context hoarding and over-delegation, and that getting value from AI agents requires the same clarity, oversight and feedback that define good people managers. [NYT Opinion, 2026-07-24]
